newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, call rate steady.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, call rate steady.

text.p: The key March three month Euroyen futures contract ended the day session firmer on Friday on technical buy-backs, while the key call rate was steady, traders said.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) maintained its less accommodative stance for the fourth straight day, underpinning the key call rate at 0.47 percent despite banks' fund demand at the final day of the one month bank reporting period.
"The call rate could have fallen below 0.40 percent this morning, but the BOJ prevented a rate tumble by not fully offsetting the market shortfall," said a senior money trader.
The BOJ left the market with a shortfall of around 90 billion yen after its regular market operation at 0020 GMT.

Its less accommodative stance has not been seen since September 1995, when the BOJ cut the discount rate and decided to let the call rate hover, on average, below the 0.5 percent discount rate, they said. In early August, the BOJ let the call rate drift below 0.40 percent for about a week, but it would not do that any longer, traders said.

"The BOJ, via its less generous fund supply, is warning the market about speculation that the Japan economy is in such a bad shape that it cannot allow any rises in short-term rates," said the first money trader.
Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) fell a real 0.7 percent in the April to June period from the previous quarter, official data showed on Friday.
This would translate into a drop of 2.9 percent on an annualised basis, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said.
In the mid-afternoon, the March was sold on a market rumour that the April-June GDP would show flat growth.
The GDP data came after the day session close.
In the night session, the key March was at 99.10 at 0702 GMT, up from 99.06 at Thursday's settlement.

On the data, Japan does not have to consider additional government spending aimed at stimulating the economy, despite a decline in gross domestic product (GDP) in the April-June quarter, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shinpei Nukaya told a news conference on Friday.
The Japanese money market and TIFFE are closed on Monday for a national holiday.
